newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds extend gains, spreads even.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds extend gains, spreads even.

text.p: Light buying helped U.S. mortgage-backeds head toward the session's close on positive ground, wiping away early losses, traders said.
Pass-through yield spreads over comparable Treasuries were mostly unchanged, they said.
"Mortgages performed fairly well today. We saw some buying in 8.0- and 8.0-percent coupons," said one Ginnie trader. Market players also scooped up zero coupon agency deals, he said.
Investors regained some bullishness after the Federal Reserve Board of Governors released its Beige Book, he said.
The Beige Book, an economic overview of the 12 Federal Reserve Bank districts, reported that the economy grew across the country in May and June but showed some pockets of weakness.
Labor markets tightened but there was "little or no wage pressure," the report said.
Traders said they read the report as confirmation that the economy is softening, which reduces the chance of another Fed hike.
"It seems like we've been wanting to trade up all day and that was just a good excuse," one trader said.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 4/32 at 100-20/32 bid, yielding 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 3/32 at 100-15/32 bid, and Freddie Mac issues also gained 3/32 at 100-20/32 bid.
The five-year Treasury note was up 4/32 to yield 6.28 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 9/32 to yield 6.39 percent.

Separately, all but one of 36 economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday and Wednesday said that Federal Reserve policymakers would leave the federal funds rate unchanged at their July 1-2 meeting. The one expert said he was undecided.
